candidates.label: SomeProducts

candidates.label: ProductGroup

Also called product family, product line, variant group. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: DrugPregnancyCategory

candidates.label: FoodService

candidates.label: State

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment

candidates.label: Occupation

candidates.label: WantAction

types.embedding_query_text: AgeGroup: A category of people defined by their age range. Also called Age bracket, Demographic, Life stage, Cohort. Examples: toddler, child, toddlers, kid.

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

types.embedding_query_text: LifeStage: A distinct period in the life cycle of an organism. Also called Developmental stage, Phase of life, Period, Epoch. Examples: first 1,000 days of a child’s life, Early childhood.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage

candidates.label: TheaterEvent

candidates.label: Schedule

candidates.label: Play

Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: BodyPart: A distinct part of an animal or human body. Also called Anatomical structure, Organ, Limb, Body region. Examples: brain.

chosen_type.label: AnatomicalStructure
chosen_type.justification: AnatomicalStructure is a direct and perfect match for 'BodyPart' and the example 'brain'.

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: AnatomicalSystem
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.

candidates.label: BrainStructure
candidates.comment: A BrainStructure is an AnatomicalStructure referring to any part of the soft nervous tissue that serves as the coordinating center for sensation, intellect, and nervous activity. Also called cerebral structure, neural component. Examples: cerebellum, hippocampus, frontal lobe, brainstem.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: Bone
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure consisting of rigid connective tissue that forms the skeletal structure of a body. Also called skeletal bone, osseous tissue. Examples: "Femur", "Skull bone", "Rib cage", "Vertebra". Distinct from Muscle, which is soft tissue for movement.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthCondition: A state of health or illness, often referring to a specific medical issue or general well-being. Also called Medical condition, Illness, Wellness, Ailment. Examples: health, inflammation, disruptions in the gut microbiome.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: MedicalCondition broadly covers states of health or illness, including specific issues like 'inflammation' and general well-being.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: HealthTopicContent
candidates.comment: HealthTopicContent is web content about a specific aspect of a health topic, such as a medical condition, its symptoms, or treatments. Also called medical web content, health information article, wellness resource. Examples: an article explaining diabetes symptoms, a webpage detailing cancer treatments, a video on heart disease prevention.

types.embedding_query_text: Diet: The kinds of food that a person, animal, or community habitually eats. Also called Eating regimen, Food intake, Nutrition plan, Eating habits. Examples: healthy diet.

chosen_type.label: Diet
chosen_type.justification: While schema.org's Diet focuses on a plan, 'healthy diet' can refer to both a habitual intake and a strategic plan, making it the closest fit.

candidates.label: Diet
candidates.comment: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: LifestyleModification
candidates.comment: A LifestyleModification is a medical entity representing a process of care involving changes to diet, exercise, and other habits to improve a health condition. Also called health habit change, wellness intervention, behavioral therapy. Examples: a weight loss program, a smoking cessation plan, a stress reduction regimen.

candidates.label: RestrictedDiet
candidates.comment: A RestrictedDiet is an Enumeration representing a diet limited to certain foods or preparations due to cultural, religious, health, or lifestyle reasons. Also called special diet, dietary restriction. Examples: vegan diet, gluten-free diet, kosher diet, low-sodium diet.

candidates.label: EatAction
candidates.comment: EatAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of swallowing solid objects. Also called consuming food, dining, ingesting. Examples: Eating a meal, consuming a snack, having dinner, biting into an apple.

types.embedding_query_text: Preference: A greater liking for one alternative over another or others. Also called Liking, Choice, Inclination, Favor. Examples: taste preferences.

candidates.label: ChooseAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or making a selection from a set of options. Also called select, pick, opt for, decide. Examples: Choosing a meal from a menu, choosing a candidate in an election, choosing a color for a car.

candidates.label: Recommendation

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: LikeAction
candidates.comment: A LikeAction is a react action representing the act of expressing a positive sentiment about an object. Also called approve action, endorse action, favorite action. Examples: liking a post on social media, giving a thumbs-up to a video, expressing approval for an idea. Distinct from DislikeAction, which expresses negative sentiment.

types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification. Also called Occupation, Career, Vocation, Field. Examples: experts.

candidates.label: Occupation

candidates.label: Specialty

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1. Also called Annual period, Calendar year, Fiscal year, Yearly cycle. Examples: 2025.

candidates.label: TVSeason

types.embedding_query_text: Regulation: A rule or directive made and maintained by an authority. Also called Rule, Law, Ordinance, Directive. Examples: mandatory, front-of-package labeling system, federal guidelines.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit

types.embedding_query_text: Industry: A group of businesses that produce a particular type of goods or services. Also called Sector, Business, Trade, Commerce. Examples: industry.

candidates.label: Occupation

candidates.label: SportsOrganization

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Brand: A type of product manufactured by a particular company under a particular name. Also called Trademark, Make, Label, Line. Examples: America’s trusted household brands.

chosen_type.label: Brand
chosen_type.justification: Brand is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and its example.

candidates.label: Brand
candidates.comment: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called Function, Capacity, Position, Duty. Examples: parents and caregivers, parents.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: Role is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and its examples 'parents and caregivers'.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

types.embedding_query_text: ProductAttribute: A characteristic or feature of a product. Also called Feature, Quality, Property, Trait. Examples: safe, affordable and convenient product choices.

chosen_type.label: PropertyValue
chosen_type.justification: PropertyValue represents a feature or characteristic of a product, which aligns with 'ProductAttribute' and its examples.

mentions: safe, affordable and convenient product choices

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

types.embedding_query_text: ConsumerNeed: A requirement or desire of a consumer that a product or service aims to satisfy. Also called Customer demand, Market need, Consumer desire, User requirement. Examples: different dietary needs, preferences and family budgets.

chosen_type.label: ConsumerNeed
chosen_type.definition: A requirement or desire of a consumer that a product or service aims to satisfy.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class directly represents 'ConsumerNeed' as an underlying requirement or desire.

mentions: different dietary needs, preferences and family budgets

candidates.label: Demand
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a public announcement by an organization or person seeking specific goods or services. Also called Request for goods, wanted ad, procurement request, call for bids. Examples: A company seeking bids for a new IT system, a person looking to buy a specific vintage car, a job posting for a software engineer. Distinct from Offer, which is an announcement to provide goods or services.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: UserReview
candidates.comment: A review or critique created by an end-user, such as a consumer or attendee, rather than a professional critic. Also called customer review, consumer feedback, public review. Examples: a customer's product review on an e-commerce site, a diner's restaurant review, an audience member's movie review. Distinct from CriticReview, which is a review written by a professional critic.

candidates.label: RestrictedDiet
candidates.comment: A RestrictedDiet is an Enumeration representing a diet limited to certain foods or preparations due to cultural, religious, health, or lifestyle reasons. Also called special diet, dietary restriction. Examples: vegan diet, gluten-free diet, kosher diet, low-sodium diet.

types.embedding_query_text: Definition: A statement of the exact meaning of a word, phrase, or concept. Also called Meaning, Explanation, Interpretation, Clarification. Examples: universally accepted scientific definition of the term ‘ultraprocessed’ food.

chosen_type.label: Statement
chosen_type.justification: A definition is a specific kind of declaration or assertion, making Statement a suitable general fit.

mentions: universally accepted scientific definition of the term ‘ultraprocessed’ food

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: MolecularEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

types.embedding_query_text: Action: The process of doing something, typically to achieve an aim. Also called Deed, Act, Operation, Activity. Examples: Cherry-picking data to fit a narrative.

chosen_type.label: Action
chosen_type.justification: Action is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and its example 'Cherry-picking data'.

mentions: Cherry-picking data to fit a narrative

candidates.label: Action
candidates.comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: FindAction
candidates.comment: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

types.embedding_query_text: Methodology: A system of methods used in a particular area of study or activity. Also called Method, Approach, Technique, Procedure. Examples: risk-based, peer-reviewed and rigorous scientific processes.

chosen_type.label: Methodology
chosen_type.definition: A system of methods used in a particular area of study or activity.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class broadly covers the concept of 'Methodology' as a system of methods.

mentions: risk-based, peer-reviewed and rigorous scientific processes

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedureType
candidates.comment: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures. Also called procedure category, intervention type, clinical technique. Examples: "DiagnosticProcedure", "TherapeuticProcedure", "SurgicalProcedure".

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center, Municipality. Examples: Austin, Texas.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: City is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and its example 'Austin, Texas'.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

types.embedding_query_text: Document: A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence or that serves as an official record. Also called Record, Text, Report, File. Examples: nutrition labels, ingredient lists.

chosen_type.label: Document
chosen_type.definition: A written, drawn, presented, or recorded representation of thought.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class broadly covers 'Document' for both physical and digital forms, such as 'nutrition labels' and 'ingredient lists'.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: SpreadsheetDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document designed for organizing and analyzing data in rows and columns, typically containing formulas and charts. Also called spreadsheet file, data sheet, workbook, Excel file. Examples: a budget spreadsheet, a sales report in Google Sheets, a financial model in Microsoft Excel.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

types.embedding_query_text: Measurement: The size, amount, or degree of something ascertained by measuring. Also called Quantity, Dimension, Extent, Value. Examples: grams of sugar, total calories.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: Measurements are expressions of measurable amounts, which directly correspond to the schema.org Quantity datatype.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common types or dimensions of measurements. Also called dimension type, measurement category, sizing parameter. Examples: "chest circumference", "inseam length", "screw gauge", "wheel diameter".

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

types.embedding_query_text: ClassificationSystem Examples: NOVA classification system, NOVA system.

chosen_type.label: CategoryCodeSet
chosen_type.justification: CategoryCodeSet explicitly mentions 'classification system' and 'taxonomy' in its definition, making it a perfect match.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: SizeSystemEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size systems used for different product categories. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, apparel sizing convention. Examples: 'US', 'UK', 'EU', 'EN-13402', 'Imperial'.

candidates.label: WearableSizeSystemEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common sizing systems specific to wearable products. Also called apparel sizing system, clothing size standard, garment measurement standard. Examples: "US size system", "EU size system", "UK size system".

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: MediaEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration providing codes and labels useful for describing media objects. Also called media classification, media type list, content category. Examples: "Video", "Audio", "Image", "Text".

types.embedding_query_text: Month: Each of the twelve periods into which a year is divided. Also called Calendar month, Period, Lunar cycle, Timeframe. Examples: January.

chosen_type.label: CalendarMonth
chosen_type.definition: Each of the twelve periods into which a year is divided.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class directly represents a calendar month as a distinct unit of time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Purpose Examples: cosmetic.

chosen_type.label: Purpose
chosen_type.definition: The reason for which something is done or created or for which something exists.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class broadly covers the abstract concept of 'Purpose'.

candidates.label: BeautySalon
candidates.comment: A HealthAndBeautyBusiness offering cosmetic treatments for hair, skin, and nails. Also called hair salon, nail salon, spa, beauty parlor. Examples: "Fantastic Sams", "Supercuts", "The Glamour Room".

candidates.label: HealthAndBeautyBusiness
candidates.comment: A HealthAndBeautyBusiness is a local business that provides services related to health and personal grooming. Also called wellness business, personal care service, aesthetic clinic. Examples: spa, gym, hair salon, nail salon, massage parlor.

candidates.label: TattooParlor
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in applying tattoos and often body piercings. Also called tattoo shop, tattoo studio, body art parlor. Examples: 'Ink Master Tattoo', 'Sacred Heart Tattoo', 'Local Tattoo & Piercing'.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: WearAction
candidates.comment: The act of dressing oneself in clothing or accessories. Also called put on, don, attire oneself. Examples: wearing a coat, putting on shoes, wearing a hat.

types.embedding_query_text: FoodPreparationMethod Examples: healthy foods at home.

chosen_type.label: FoodPreparationMethod
chosen_type.definition: A technique or process used to prepare food for consumption.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class directly represents a 'FoodPreparationMethod'.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: NutritionInformation
candidates.comment: NutritionInformation, as a StructuredValue, provides details about the nutritional content of food, often for a recipe. Also called nutritional facts, food label information, dietary data. Examples: calorie count, fat content, protein amount, vitamin percentages. Distinct from Recipe, which describes how to prepare food.

candidates.label: FastFoodRestaurant
candidates.comment: A FastFoodRestaurant is a FoodEstablishment specializing in quickly prepared and served food. Also called quick-service restaurant, drive-thru. Examples: McDonald's, Subway, a local burger joint, a taco stand.

candidates.label: FoodEstablishmentReservation
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishmentReservation is a Reservation to dine at a food-related business. Also called restaurant booking, table reservation, dining reservation. Examples: A confirmed table booking at a restaurant, a reservation for a cafe, a booking for a private dining event. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tables for booking.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.
